signals.entity: ELTA (Hellenic Post) — cash-counting estate, wider picture
signals.signal: Diavgeia holds a continuous 2026 stream of ELTA 'Repair-Maintenance of Office Machines' decisions covering banknote counters, all below threshold and all via direct award: CashDNA TN10 batches on 05/02/2026 (ΡΗ2ΩΟΡΡ2-0ΜΑ), 04/03/2026 (93ΒΥΟΡΡ2-ΓΘΖ), 03/04/2026 (Ψ4ΠΖΟΡΡ2-ΦΤΘ), 11/06/2026 (ΡΒ2ΖΟΡΡ2-ΙΗΔ, covering two periods 17.03-01.04 and 02.04-19.05.2026) and 17/07/2026; plus a NC6500 counter at an ELTA branch on 20/04/2026 (9Λ81ΟΡΡ2-0ΡΖ) and a SCANCOIN counter at the Patra cash centre on 25/05/2026 (ΨΨΡΥΟΡΡ2-2ΞΣ). signals.implies: A fragmented, multi-vendor, ageing counter estate maintained incident-by-incident is expensive and un-auditable. It also maps directly to the ELTA all-bank ATM network idea, where Printec Cash Network/Cashflex is the natural vehicle.

signals.followup: Quantify the ELTA counter estate (how many TN10 serials appear across all 2026 decisions) to size a refresh; check ELTA's 2026 investment plan for cash-centre automation.

signals.entity: Municipality of Mykonos — independent ATM deployers
signals.signal: Municipal Council decision 35/2026 of 02/03/2026 (session 4/02-03-2026), taken unanimously, on the agenda item 'uncontrolled installation of Automatic Teller Machines (ATMs) in and outside the town-plan areas of Mykonos'. It (1) enforces the full permitting checklist set out by the Mykonos planning department for ATMs on public/communal land — application, Municipal Committee decision, building permit or small-scale-works approval, topographic and layout drawings, Architectural Council approval, Archaeology approval, aesthetic/planning limits, public-space usage fee, and an installer's electrical declaration, with a parallel checklist for ATMs on private shop/hotel facades; (2) orders the planning department to inspect and record all ATMs that visibly offend public space or the architecture of the landscape and to impose planning sanctions, notifying the Mykonos Police Sub-directorate; and (3) orders the ATM-installing company/companies to be formally notified and audited for compliance. Legal basis cited: arts. 8, 9 and 26 of L.5056/2023 and Interior Ministry circular 1328/110575/2023.
signals.source_name: Diavgeia — Municipality of Mykonos decision ADA 6ΣΚ4ΩΚΚ-ΔΗ4 (PDF); community opinion 03/2026 ADA 6ΜΤΝΩΚΚ-3ΧΧ
signals.implies: A Greek tourist municipality is moving to police independent ATM deployers with planning sanctions and police referral. That is a regulatory squeeze on the unbranded island ATM estate (the high-fee/DCC operator model) and it raises the value of a compliant, permitted, well-integrated operator. Printec Cash Network / Cashflex, already running ~850 off-site ATMs in Greece, can position as the compliant alternative and pick up sites that non-compliant deployers are forced to remove. Also a live risk to check for any Printec-operated sites on Mykonos.
signals.likelihood: High that inspections proceed on Mykonos; Medium that other Cyclades/tourist municipalities copy it within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Identify which deployer(s) the decision targets and whether any Cashflex/Printec Cash Network sites on Mykonos are exposed; watch other island municipalities for copycat decisions; build a permitting/compliance pack as a sales asset.

signals.entity: Off-site ATM siting across Greek municipalities (Chalkida, Preveza, Zografou, Pogoniou)
signals.signal: Four municipal decisions in a five-month window all turn on where off-site ATMs sit and who pays for them: Chalkida Municipal Council decision 48/2026 of 06/04/2026 unanimously approves installing a cash-withdrawal ATM in the Nea Lampsakos community, the recommendation arguing that relief from 'the complete lack of access to banking services' is not a luxury but a necessity, with the municipality to choose a suitable and safe site; Preveza decision 53/2026 of 30/03/2026 waives the rent on Trapeza Ipeirou's Louros ATM; a Zografou decision of 09/07/2026 concerns leasing space for an Alpha Bank cash-withdrawal ATM (ADA ΡΘ2ΛΩΡΦ-ΑΓΖ); and a Pogoniou decision of 14/07/2026 grants use of part of a communal square in a municipal community for ATM siting (ADA 96ΜΣΩ1Ω-Υ1Π, Piraeus Bank).
signals.source_name: Diavgeia — Municipality of Chalkida decision ADA 9ΒΖΥΩΗΑ-7Φ7 (PDF), corroborated by Diavgeia Tier-0 cache rows ΡΘ2ΛΩΡΦ-ΑΓΖ and 96ΜΣΩ1Ω-Υ1Π
signals.implies: Greek municipalities are now actively demanding ATMs (Chalkida), subsidising them (Preveza) and brokering bank leases (Zografou, Pogoniou) — the branch-closure gap is being filled at municipal level, one site at a time, with the municipality supplying free or cheap space. This is the demand base for an outsourced off-site ATM network: Printec Cash Network / Cashflex can aggregate exactly these single-site, sub-scale requests that no individual bank will fund alone. Product fit: ATM/self-service plus managed services, CIT route optimisation, and recyclers where deposit volume justifies them.

signals.followup: Stand up a rolling Diavgeia query on municipal ATM siting/lease/waiver decisions to produce a live Greek off-site ATM demand map and hand it to Cashflex/Printec Cash Network as a site-acquisition pipeline; identify which bank is behind the Chalkida request.

signals.entity: Greek public-sector cash-equipment direct-award channel (competitor mapping)
signals.signal: Diavgeia shows a consistent pattern of Greek public bodies buying counting and counterfeit-detection hardware by direct award under art. 118 L.4412/2016, from small local traders and specialist resellers rather than through tenders. Verified: Municipality of Tripoli, Mayor's decision 9929 of 03/04/2026, awards a 'banknote detection and counting device' to Ms Panopoulou Maria, Spetseropoulou 30, Tripoli, AFM 061943464, for EUR 347.20 incl. The Tier-0 Diavgeia cache shows the same pattern at water utilities: Pylos-Nestor DEYA counterfeit detector with counting on 05/02/2026 (ADA 90ΖΨΟΕ3Υ-Κ2Ε) and again 23/03/2026 (ADA Ρ4ΑΖΟΕ3Υ-ΒΩ8); a direct award for two counting machines on 17/02/2026 (ADA ΨΡ6ΝΟΡΝΗ-ΑΜΞ); and Florina DEYA renewing an ANNUAL MAINTENANCE contract on two counting machines on 15/04/2026 (ADA Ψ698ΟΕΕΖ-ΛΓΚ).
signals.source_name: Diavgeia — Municipality of Tripoli award decision ADA 90ΕΘΩΗΡ-ΖΓΛ (PDF), plus Tier-0 cache greek_tenders_diavgeia.json
signals.implies: The Greek public cash-equipment market is a long tail of sub-EUR-2,000 direct awards that never reach KIMDIS/ESIDIS competition, so it is invisible to tender monitoring and is being taken by micro-resellers. Individually trivial, collectively a steady annual volume and — more valuable — an installed base that generates recurring maintenance contracts, as the Florina annual contract proves. Printec's realistic play is not to bid these but to become the default name on three-quote lists and to sell the service wrap.
signals.likelihood: High — continuous, several decisions per month
signals.followup: Run a monthly Diavgeia direct-award sweep on the counting/detection CPVs (35121200-0, 30123600) to size the annual long-tail spend and name every recurring supplier for Agent 6's competitor file.

The stated vision is a transition to a modern company of services, logistics and commercial activities and the creation of a leading service platform for citizens and businesses in Greece, explicitly leveraging modern financial services. The press report carries no investment figures and no ATM, cash-handling or self-service specifics.

If ELTA builds out post-office financial services across its nationwide network it needs cash automation, self-service terminals and an ATM proposition — the exact package Printec sells, and the natural vehicle is Printec Cash Network / Cashflex for an all-bank ELTA ATM network. Treat as pipeline, not a tender.

signals.followup: Obtain the actual ELTA 2026-2030 plan document (not the press summary) and its capex annex from ELTA or the Growthfund/Superfund, and establish whether 'financial services' means cash/ATM infrastructure or agency banking only. This is the highest-value unresolved question on the Greek beat.

signals.entity: ELTA (Hellenic Post) / BOOS S.A. — tender 3726 AWARD
signals.signal: ELTA Executive Committee decision A.P. 274 of 21/05/2026 (session 82/19-05-2026, item 1) AWARDS open competitive procedure 3726 for the operational leasing of 300 banknote counting and QUALITY-SORTING machines, 5-year term, with an option for 200 additional machines, to BOOS S.A. (SYSTIMATA ORGANOSEOS TRAPEZON KAI GRAFEION A.E. - Idiotiki Epicheirisi Parochis Ypiresion Asfaleias), Leoforos Mesogeion 262, 15562 Cholargos, AFM 095053250, GEMI 008820701000. Price: EUR 19.25 per machine per month excl. VAT, i.e. EUR 346,500.00 excl. VAT for 300 machines over the 5 years, against an approved budget of EUR 885,000.00 excl. VAT (EUR 1,097,400.00 incl. VAT 24%) set by decision A.P. 244 of 23/03/2026 (session 74/17-03-2026, ADA ΨΓ14ΟΡΡ2-Ο38), CPV 66114000-2, award criterion lowest price. The machines are Double Power model DF-8150F, ECB-certified for counterfeit detection and fitness sorting. Three bidders competed: BOOS S.A., Ch. THEODOSIS A.B.E.E. and IBANDO (IB&O Intelligent Bank & Office Machines - V. Papadatos & Sia E.E.). The contractor bears all maintenance labour and parts except misuse; misuse rates are EUR 55.00 first hour in its workshop, EUR 25.00 each subsequent hour, EUR 75.00 first hour at ELTA's Kryoneri central warehouse, EUR 30.00 each subsequent. Guarantee is 3 months' rent (EUR 17,325.00, confirmed paid by ELTA decision ADA ΨΜ7ΒΟΡΡ2-ΝΕΑ of 22/05/2026); early termination costs half the remaining rents; the option's 200 extra machines would add EUR 3,850.00 per month excl. VAT. Critically, the decision states the award discharges an obligation arising from ELTA's Cooperation Agreement with the bank EUROBANK as amended on 30/04/2025.
signals.source_name: Diavgeia — ELTA Executive Committee award decision ADA Ψ6ΓΨΟΡΡ2-ΥΟΡ (PDF, extracted locally)
signals.implies: This is the Greek cash-automation deal of the cycle and Printec was not in it. It overturns two prior readings: the ELTA counter refresh was NOT merely 'plausible but unadvertised' — it was tendered and awarded; and Greek public buyers ARE now buying fitness-SORTING, not just counting. BOOS S.A. converts from a per-incident break-fix supplier under the 2016 contract into a 5-year, 300-500 machine managed-lease incumbent across ELTA's counter network, with maintenance bundled — precisely Printec's own managed-services model, sold at EUR 19.25/machine/month. The Eurobank clause is the strategic tell: ELTA's counter equipment is being specified to serve Eurobank agency banking, so the ELTA banking build-out has a named bank sponsor and a live equipment channel. Printec product fit: cash automation/recyclers, teller counting and managed services.
signals.likelihood: Contract is awarded and guaranteed; the 200-machine option is the next decision point and is live now
signals.followup: Establish whether the 200-machine option has been exercised and on what trigger; benchmark Printec against EUR 19.25/machine/month bundled-maintenance economics; profile Double Power DF-8150F and BOOS S.A.'s distribution rights for Agent 6; and target the NEXT ELTA equipment wave (recyclers/ATMs) rather than this counter lease. Also profile the two losing bidders IBANDO (V. Papadatos & Sia E.E.) and Ch. THEODOSIS A.B.E.E.

signals.entity: ELTA (Hellenic Post) — all-bank fee-free ATM plan
signals.signal: Reporting of 18/02/2026 on the ELTA transformation, run under Ministry of National Economy minister Kyriakos Pierrakakis, states that roughly 450 ELTA locations already provide basic banking services out of an active network of 985 points, that pilot expanded-banking operations have started at Aliartos and Messini, and that the plan provides for account opening, deposits and withdrawals, bill payments and AT MINIMUM ONE ATM PER LOCATION SERVING ALL BANKS WITHOUT FEES where no alternative cash access exists. The same report records 11 regional branch closures with a further 30 planned for March. Cooperation is described as involving more than one banking institution; no investment figure is given.
signals.source_name: Olympio Vima — 'Νέος ρόλος για ΕΛΤΑ με ΑΤΜ και τραπεζικά γκισέ'
signals.implies: This answers the biggest open question on the Greek beat: ELTA 'financial services' explicitly includes ATM hardware, not just agency banking over the counter. A multi-bank, fee-free ATM at up to ~450-985 postal locations is the largest identifiable Greek self-service opportunity in this cycle, and an interbank-shared, fee-free estate is exactly the independent-operator model rather than a single bank's own fleet. Printec Cash Network / Cashflex (80.10%, ~850 off-site ATMs) is the natural vehicle. It also explains the municipal ATM-siting and rent-waiver decisions logged this run: rural cash access is being solved politically, and ELTA is the designated instrument.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that an ATM supply or ATM-as-a-service procurement follows within 6-12 months; the counter-equipment lease already awarded shows ELTA is executing the plan through real tenders
signals.followup: Confirm the ATM commitment against a primary ELTA/Ministry document rather than press, and establish whether ATMs will be bought, leased or taken as a managed service, and which banks join the fee-free scheme. Watch ELTA's KIMDIS notices via contracts.gr org 50039. This is the single highest-value item for Printec Cash Network.

signals.entity: ODAP / Visa / Cardlink (a Worldline brand) — 22 ticket machines already contracted
signals.signal: ODAP announced on 28/08/2025 a FIVE-YEAR extension of its cooperation with Visa and Cardlink (a Worldline brand) to install 22 additional automatic ticket-vending machines at archaeological sites and museums including Sounion, the Olympieion, the Ancient Agora of Athens, Mystras, Delos, Spinalonga, Ancient Corinth and Aigai, building on machines installed in 2023 at the Acropolis, Ancient Olympia, Epidaurus and Delphi, where over 200,000 tickets were issued at the Acropolis alone in about 18 months. The machines are card-only; Cardlink supplies acceptance/acquiring and Visa the security standards. No contract value is disclosed. Separately, KIMDIS notice 25PROC016452145 of 12/03/2025 records an ODAP procurement under CPV 30144200-2 (ticket-issuing machines) valued at EUR 1,295,800.00, and the Ministry of Culture published notice 26PROC018725807 of 27/03/2026 for e-ticket equipment worth EUR 14,999.99 for Kalymnos, Karpathos, Kos and Rhodes.
signals.source_name: ODAP press release (odap.gr), corroborated by Cardlink and by contracts.gr KIMDIS index for CPV 30144200-2
signals.implies: MATERIAL CORRECTION to this run's earlier ODAP reading. The EUR 37,200 ODAP siting study of 25/02/2026 for 22 ticket machines is NOT the precursor to an open supply tender — the same 22 machines are already covered by a five-year Visa/Cardlink arrangement announced in August 2025, so the study is siting work inside a contract Printec cannot bid. The lane is closed for five years and Cardlink/Worldline is consolidating unattended public payment acceptance in Greece, having also supplied POS to the Chania Port Fund. The residual openings are the hardware layer (kiosk supply, cash-accepting variants, field service) and the fact that card-only machines leave cash-paying visitors unserved.
signals.likelihood: High that the Cardlink/Visa arrangement runs to term; Low that an open ODAP ticket-machine supply tender appears in 6-12 months
signals.followup: Obtain notice 25PROC016452145 to see whether the EUR 1,295,800 was competitively tendered and who won; establish who manufactures the kiosks behind the Cardlink arrangement and whether field service is subcontracted — that is the realistic Printec entry point.

signals.entity: KIMDIS/ESIDIS access route — contracts.gr index (coverage finding)
signals.signal: The Greek national procurement portal promitheus.gov.gr redirects (HTTP 302) to portal.eprocurement.gov.gr, which returns an empty body to a plain fetch because it is a JavaScript application, and per-CPV paths on it are not directly fetchable. A working substitute index was established this run: contracts.gr exposes KIMDIS/ESIDIS/Diavgeia notices at stable per-CPV URLs of the form https://www.contracts.gr/v1/cpv/code/<CPV> and per-organisation URLs of the form https://www.contracts.gr/v1/orgs/<id> (ELTA is 50039, ELTA Courier 50096), returning KIMDIS reference numbers (25PROC…/26PROC…), authority, title, value and date. This is how the ELTA 300-machine lease and award, invisible in the Tier-0 Diavgeia cache triage, were found.
signals.implies: Closes the largest stated coverage gap on this beat: above-threshold Greek notices are now reachable. It also shows the Tier-0 Diavgeia keyword cache under-reports the material deals — the EUR 885,000 ELTA lease and its award were absent from it — so future runs must query by CPV and by organisation, not only by subject keyword. Practical effect for Printec: a monitorable pipeline of Greek ATM/POS/cash-automation notices.
signals.likelihood: Route is live and stable now
signals.followup: Add contracts.gr per-CPV monitoring for 66114000-2, 35121200-0, 30144200-2, 30123600-2, 50310000-1, 42933000-5 and per-organisation monitoring for ELTA (50039), ODAP and Tameio Parakatathikon; treat every hit as a lead requiring Diavgeia/KIMDIS primary verification.

signals.entity: ELTA / Eurobank agency-banking network (demand driver behind the counter-equipment lease)
signals.signal: Eurobank operates a public 'ELTA branch network' service page listing the ELTA post offices where Eurobank customers can transact; the page states the list reflects the recent ELTA network reorganisation and that available services include opening deposit and fixed-term accounts, issuing debit cards, CASH WITHDRAWALS AND DEPOSITS, loan repayments, salary/pension crediting and customer onboarding/KYC updates. This is the same Cooperation Agreement, as amended on 30/04/2025, that ELTA's own award decision of 21/05/2026 cites as the obligation requiring the 300 banknote counting and fitness-sorting machines. Press reporting in the same period describes ELTA branch closures (204 branches cited) and continuing cooperations with both Eurobank and Alpha Bank.
signals.implies: Confirms from the bank's own side that ELTA post offices are already live cash-handling banking points doing deposits and withdrawals, and that onboarding/KYC happens at the counter. Two Printec lines map directly: cash automation (the counter equipment is being re-fleeted right now, and deposit-taking counters are the natural place for recyclers rather than plain sorters) and digital onboarding/eKYC plus AML/compliance for account opening performed by postal staff rather than bankers — a control gap a bank must close. It also sets the commercial frame for the all-bank fee-free ATM plan: agency banking at the counter is phase one, self-service is phase two.
signals.likelihood: Live now and expanding through 2026 as branches are reorganised
signals.followup: Get the ELTA-Eurobank Cooperation Agreement amendment of 30/04/2025 to see what equipment and compliance obligations it imposes on ELTA; pitch eKYC/AML tooling for postal-counter onboarding and recyclers for deposit-taking counters; confirm Alpha Bank's parallel arrangement.

coverage_notes:
RETRY ROUND 1, RESUMED FROM CHECKPOINT AND THEN EXTENDED. Step 0 found an existing checkpoint for this same runDate (2026-08-01) with status 'complete' and 14 signals, so the retry brief's premise that the first pass 'returned NOTHING' is contradicted by what is on disk — the earlier research did complete and is preserved unchanged here (a .json.bak backup was taken first). Rather than stop there, this round attacked the checkpoint's single stated gap: KIMDIS/ESIDIS had never been searched directly because promitheus.gov.gr was unreachable. That gap is now CLOSED, and closing it produced the most important Greek finding of the cycle.

NEW THIS ROUND (5 signals appended, 19 total). (1) Access breakthrough: promitheus.gov.gr 302-redirects to portal.eprocurement.gov.gr, which is a JS app returning an empty body to a plain fetch; the working substitute is contracts.gr, which indexes KIMDIS/ESIDIS/Diavgeia at stable per-CPV (/v1/cpv/code/<CPV>) and per-organisation (/v1/orgs/<id>) URLs and returns 25PROC/26PROC KIMDIS reference numbers. CPVs swept: 35121200-0 (counterfeit detectors), 30144200-2 (ticket-issuing machines), 42933000-5 (vending machines), 50310000-1 (office-machine maintenance); 30123600-2 returns 404/500 on both the plain and /related paths and is logged as unresolved. (2) The headline find: ELTA open competitive procedure 3726 for the operational leasing of 300 banknote counting AND QUALITY-SORTING machines (option +200), 5 years, budget EUR 885,000 excl. VAT (= EUR 1,097,400 incl. VAT 24%), AWARDED 21/05/2026 to BOOS S.A. (AFM 095053250) at EUR 19.25/machine/month, EUR 346,500 excl. VAT total, machines Double Power DF-8150F, ECB-certified. Three bidders named. Both the launch decision (ADA ΨΓ14ΟΡΡ2-Ο38) and the award (ADA Ψ6ΓΨΟΡΡ2-ΥΟΡ) were downloaded as PDFs and extracted locally with pdfminer.six, and the EUR 17,325 guarantee decision (ADA ΨΜ7ΒΟΡΡ2-ΝΕΑ) independently reconciles as exactly 3 months' rent (3 x 19.25 x 300). (3) ELTA's ATM intent is now on the record: reporting of 18/02/2026 states the plan provides at minimum one ATM per location serving ALL banks WITHOUT fees, with ~450 of 985 active ELTA points already doing basic banking and pilots at Aliartos and Messini. (4) MATERIAL CORRECTION: the ODAP 22 ticket-vending machines are already inside a five-year ODAP/Visa/Cardlink (Worldline) arrangement announced 28/08/2025, so the EUR 37,200 siting study reported earlier is work inside a closed contract, not the precursor to an open supply tender; the two affected earlier signals were amended in place rather than deleted. (5) Eurobank's own ELTA-network page confirms deposits, withdrawals, debit-card issuance and customer onboarding at postal counters, which is the contractual driver the ELTA award decision cites.

TWO EARLIER CONCLUSIONS ARE NOW OVERTURNED and should not be carried forward: the earlier note that Greek sweeps for banknote SORTING returned ZERO and that Greek public buyers buy only simple counters is WRONG — a 300-to-500 machine fitness-sorting deal was running the whole time; and the earlier read that an ELTA fleet refresh was 'plausible but not yet advertised' is WRONG — it was tendered, awarded and guaranteed between March and May 2026. Both were missed because the Tier-0 Diavgeia keyword cache does not contain them, which is the methodological lesson: query Greek procurement by CPV and by organisation, not only by subject keyword.

REMAINING GAPS: whether ELTA has exercised the 200-machine option is unknown; the ODAP KIMDIS notice 25PROC016452145 (EUR 1,295,800, modification of 25PROC016252913) names no winner on the aggregator and the underlying award was not located; CPV 30123600-2 could not be listed; and Greek commercial banks (Piraeus, Alpha, Eurobank, NBG) remain structurally invisible because they are private and publish no procurement notices — that remains a finding, not a fixable gap.
access_issues: promitheus.gov.gr returns HTTP 302 to portal.eprocurement.gov.gr, which renders an empty body to a plain fetch (JavaScript application) — logged, not silently dropped; the working substitute route is contracts.gr per-CPV and per-organisation URLs. contracts.gr itself returns HTTP 404 on /v1/cpv/code/30123600-2 and /v1/cpv/code/30123600 and HTTP 500 on /v1/cpv/code/30123600-2/related, so coin/banknote-handling machinery could not be listed by CPV this round. api.diavgeia.gov.gr does not resolve from this host (DNS ENOTFOUND); the et.diavgeia.gov.gr/luminapi/api/search/export route surfaced in search results but returned HTTP 400 to the query form tried, so per-organisation Diavgeia API filtering remains UNPROVEN. The working Diavgeia routes stay https://diavgeia.gov.gr/opendata/search.json?subject=<term> for listing and https://diavgeia.gov.gr/doc/<ADA> for documents; diavgeia.gov.gr/doc serves binary PDFs the fetch tool cannot read, but it saves them to disk and pdfminer.six extracts them cleanly (system pdftotext is NOT installed) — this is how both ELTA decisions were read. One Diavgeia doc URL (ADA ΨΜ7ΒΟΡΡ2-ΝΕΑ) 302-redirected to http://static.old.diavgeia.gov.gr/doc/<ADA>, a second host worth knowing. Bash has no network access on this host, so all fetching went through WebFetch. www.bankofgreece.gr/enimerosi/prokhryxeis remains HTTP 404; the live route is the announcements search. Claude-in-Chrome was not required this round because the JS block on portal.eprocurement.gov.gr was routed around via contracts.gr rather than escalated. DATE CAUTION: the Eurobank ELTA-network page's stated reorganisation date rendered inconsistently across retrievals (06.07.2026 in one snapshot, 03.08.2026 in another, the latter being after this runDate), so no reorganisation date is asserted in the signal and the access date 01/08/2026 is used instead.
